flashcards.q: content-box vs border-box: width:200px, padding:20px, border:5px -- what's the rendered width for each?
flashcards.a: content-box (spec default): 250px total (200 content + 40 padding + 10 border, added on top). border-box: exactly 200px total -- content area shrinks to 150px to accommodate padding/border.

flashcards.q: What's the decision rule for Flexbox vs Grid?
flashcards.a: If items need to align across BOTH rows and columns simultaneously, use Grid. If distributing/aligning along a single row or column with wrapping as a secondary concern, use Flexbox. They compose freely.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't z-index:9999 always win against a sibling with z-index:1?
flashcards.a: z-index only compares elements within the SAME stacking context. If the high z-index element is trapped inside an ancestor that created its own stacking context, it can never beat something entirely outside that context, regardless of the number.

flashcards.q: List properties/conditions that create a new stacking context.
flashcards.a: position:fixed/sticky (always); position:relative/absolute + non-auto z-index; opacity<1; transform!=none; filter/backdrop-filter!=none; will-change naming a triggering property; isolation:isolate; flex/grid item with non-auto z-index.

flashcards.q: What is the containing block for position:absolute, and what can override position:fixed's normal viewport-relative containing block?
flashcards.a: Nearest ancestor with position != static. For position:fixed (normally viewport-relative), a transform, filter, will-change:transform, perspective, or contain:layout on ANY ancestor establishes a new containing block instead of the viewport.

flashcards.q: Difference between media queries and container queries?
flashcards.a: Media queries respond only to viewport dimensions. Container queries (container-type:inline-size + @container) respond to the actual size of a specific ancestor container, regardless of viewport width -- needed for components reused in different-width contexts.

Adjacent VERTICAL margins between block-level siblings in normal flow collapse to the LARGER value, not the sum. margin-bottom:20px followed by margin-top:30px produces a 30px gap, not 50px. Doesn't apply horizontally or to flex/grid children.

flashcards.q: What are logical properties and why use them?
flashcards.a: Flow-relative properties like margin-inline-start / padding-block-end that map to physical directions based on writing mode/direction -- automatically correct for RTL languages and vertical writing modes without a parallel override stylesheet.

flashcards.q: What does isolation:isolate do and what's its risk?
flashcards.a: Forces a new stacking context without needing another side-effecting property like opacity or transform -- used to sandbox a component's internal z-index values. Risk: it can trap content that legitimately needs to stack above something outside its own subtree, the same boundary problem it was meant to prevent.

flashcards.q: As of 2026, what's the browser support status for container queries and :has()?
flashcards.a: Both have full support across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari as of 2026 and are considered safe for production use.
